newsitem.title: EGYPT: EU Mideast envoy off to see Ross on upbeat note.
newsitem.headline: EU Mideast envoy off to see Ross on upbeat note.

text.p: European Union special envoy Miguel Angel Moratinos left Cairo for talks in the United States on Thursday in a cautiously optimistic mood about diplomatic attempts to break the deadlock in Middle East peace talks.

"I cannot speak of proposals but I can confirm to you that there is the beginning of a solution but only a beginning. It is not yet a solution," he told reporters on Wednesday night after talks with Egyptian Foreign Minister Amr Moussa.
The thrust of the Egyptian-led diplomacy is to reconcile differences between Israel and the Palestinians over a Jewish settlement Israel is building in Arab East Jerusalem.

Palestinian President Yasser Arafat has refused to meet Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu since Israel decided in March to go ahead with the settlement. Substantial talks on the next stages of the peace process have collapsed.

Moratinos, who saw Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy in Israel on Tuesday, said: "In the last weeks we have noticed -- the European Union and the Egyptian authorities -- that there is a little opening on the part of the Israeli prime minister, a desire to get out of the deadlock."
"There has been some openness but still there is some work to be done," the envoy added.

He said that in the United States he would meet the U.S. special envoy on the Middle East, Dennis Ross. "We will exchange points of view and see if in the present context there should be a new (European-American) initiative in parallel," he added.

Egyptian presidential adviser Osama el-Baz, one of the key players in the mediation attempt, is also in the United States. Egyptian government newspapers said he would meet U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright on Friday.
In Cairo on Wednesday Moratinos had talks with President Hosni Mubarak, who also saw Arafat. Mubarak had an inconclusive meeting with Netanyahu in the Egyptian resort of Sharm el-Sheikh last week.

Moratinos told reporters that the European Union did not have its own Middle East initiative. "We are supporting the Egyptian role now. We are leaving the Egyptian diplomacy time for success and supporting any decisions that are going to be taken...," he said.
Arafat returned to Gaza on Wednesday and Moratinos said he and his ministers would discuss a response to unspecified Israeli and Egyptian ideas.
